_doc: TEACH-BACK CONTENT — placeholder authored by the systems coder so the engine + tests run. The content coder's file REPLACES this one; keep the schema EXACT: { questions: [{ id, conceptId, asker: 'rivet'|'bolt'|'juno'|'magma'|'spark', naiveQuestion, options: [{ text, correct, misconception }] (1 correct + 2 wrong, each wrong tagged with the misconception it reveals), taughtLine, retryLine }] }. conceptId must be one of the 16 fixed ids in src/learning/concepts.js.

questions.naiveQuestion: The if tile has two mouths. Which one eats the answer when the sensor says TRUE?

options.text: The THEN mouth — it runs when the condition is TRUE
The ELSE mouth — that one gets the true stuff
Both mouths run every loop, one after the other

questions.taughtLine: Exactly — THEN is the true road. You just taught a robot to choose.
questions.retryLine: Close! THEN is the road the robot takes when the condition is TRUE. ELSE is the other one.

questions.naiveQuestion: My drive-to-the-wall program loops forever and never parks. What does it need?

options.text: An exit — a break (or repeat-until) for when the wall is close
A bigger forever loop — forever twice is more stopping
Nothing, forever loops stop themselves when they get tired

questions.taughtLine: That's it — every forever needs a way out. The wall was telling it to stop all along.
questions.retryLine: Think again: a forever loop runs FOREVER. It stops when YOU build the exit — break or repeat-until.

questions.naiveQuestion: How does the robot even KNOW things? It doesn't have eyes. Or does it?

options.text: Sensors — parts that turn the world into numbers the program can read
It guesses from how the motors feel
The flashlight tells it what to do directly

questions.taughtLine: Yes — a sensor is how a robot asks the world a question, and readings are the answers.
questions.retryLine: Not quite — motors and lights are OUTPUTS. Sensors are the inputs: parts that turn the world into numbers.
